item.title: Live: Iran's Guards threaten US sites in the region if its tankers come under fire
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have threatened to target US sites in the Middle East if its tankers come under fire, Iranian media reported on Saturday, as Washington continued to wait for Tehran’s response to its latest proposal for a peace deal. Follow our live blog for all the latest updates.

item.title: Middle East war back on? UAE responds to fresh attacks, US and Iran trade fire
item.description: The United Arab Emirates says it's responded to fresh missile and drone attacks by Iran this Friday. The strikes come hours after the US says three of its navy destroyers in the Strait of Hormuz were targeted. President Donald Trump ordered retaliatory strikes - but then downplayed the hostilities and said the ceasefire still stands. Analysis by Douglas Herbert, FRANCE 24 international affairs commentator.

item.title: Israel Says It Killed a Hezbollah Chief Near Beirut, Testing the Truce
item.description: The strike was the first near the Lebanese capital since a cease-fire that has curbed fighting but not halted it. Washington is pushing for a lasting peace, hoping it will ease diplomacy with Iran.

item.title: Iran keeps US waiting for response on ceasefire plan
item.description: Iran on Saturday questioned the seriousness of US diplomacy while keeping Washington waiting for a response to its latest negotiating position in the wake of renewed naval clashes in the Gulf. A parallel ceasefire on the war's Lebanon front is also under strain amid daily exchanges of fire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah.

item.title: What we know about the latest exchange of fire between the US and Iran
item.description: US president Donald Trump insisted the ceasefire with Iran was still in place Thursday, despite an exchange of fire with Iranian forces in the Strait of Hormuz. The US and Iran offered conflicting views of the event - as both nations claimed to have been targeted first. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran.

item.title: Israel launches strikes on south Lebanon after warning residents to evacuate
item.description: The Israeli military launched strikes across southern Lebanon on Saturday after issuing evacuation warnings for several villages in the area, saying it was targeting Hezbollah positions despite an existing ceasefire.

item.title: Sporadic clashes erupt between ‌Iranian and US forces ‌in Hormuz strait
item.description: Sporadic clashes erupted between Iranian and US forces on Friday in the Strait of Hormuz after the US fired at two empty oil tankers trying to break the blockade by heading for an empty Iranian port in the Gulf of Oman, the American military said. Late on Friday, the US and Iran also traded fire in the first real challenge to the fragile ceasefire. Read our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Iran warns the US against attacks on its oil tankers and other ships but ceasefire appears to hold
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy has warned of a “heavy assault” on one of the U.S. bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers or commercial vessels are attacked

item.title: One Page Peace Plan for Iran? Starmer’s Sinking Ship, Musk V Altman
item.description: In a week thats’s seen renewed hope for ending the war in Iran, ten weeks since it started, with four weeks of stalemate, a ceasefire and skirmishes over the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Intermittent peace talks have boiled down to a fourteen-point, one-page “memorandum of understanding”, crafted by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, which has been sent to Pakistani mediators and is being reviewed by Iran.
